text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.83% today, a modest gain that comes after the stock had fallen 8.4% over the past two weeks. The slight rebound today follows yesterday's dip and tracks alongside oil prices: US crude is holding around $99.60 per barrel, while Brent (the global benchmark) recently dipped below $90 for the first time since August. That dip reflects easing geopolitical tension—Trump indicated the Iran conflict may be ending soon, which typically pushes oil prices down as traders bet on fewer supply disruptions ahead.

The two-week decline likely reflects that same shift in expectations. When oil prices fall, companies that profit from producing or refining crude tend to sell off, since their revenues are directly tied to what they can get paid per barrel. ConocoPhillips' recent earnings report (posted November 5th) provided a baseline, but the bigger driver has been the market's recalibration of oil prices as the outlook for the Iran situation brightened.
